prompt: Sofia's four-week project plan fills every day exactly, with each stage starting the day the previous one ends and no slack. In week two one task takes two extra days and the whole plan collapses. What planning error does this show?

options.text: She planned the project in too much detail
She should have worked weekends from the start
Estimates are usually optimistic, so a workable plan needs buffer time and a decision about what can be dropped if things slip
A four-week project should never be split into stages

explanation: This is the planning fallacy in action: single-point optimistic estimates with zero slack. Buffers and a pre-chosen drop-list turn a slip into an adjustment instead of a collapse.
